scope: REA decompilation of synthetic instruction-span analysis functions inside original FDE 0x9b0c650. These are not original native entries or a whole report decompilation. Caller/stack context is absent; Ghidra may follow neighboring copied page bytes beyond the declared span. Behavioral claims rely on original assembly and actual bounded replay.

projection.provenance: Non-executable analysis projection of the fixed ELF. Selected original instruction bytes match original SHA-256. Full FDEs and instruction spans are identified separately; a span's declared function is synthetic, its original caller/stack context and control flow outside the span are absent. Referenced RIP data pages copied at original VAs. Synthetic ELF header and symbols; original sections, unwind metadata, dynamic relocations, and most callees omitted. Check every semantic conclusion against original assembly or isolated replay.

limitations: The session serves operations only after Ghidra reports default auto-analysis complete; incomplete analysis does not expose partial results.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
Pseudocode is Ghidra decompiler output, not original source and not text-equivalent to Hopper output.
External functions and functions without an analyzable body return null; other decompiler failures remain explicit.
